claim: Good non-protected non-demon kills reduce health by role damage, while Evil characters independently add unrevealed-count plus five gold.
The Health wrappers dispatch Reduce, Add, and Reset, and CurrentMaxValue.GetValue reads current at +0x1C; shared native bodies are recorded explicitly.
AddMaxHp increments CurrentMaxValue.max, dispatches Add, then explicitly raises the value-change and UI-update delegates when present.
Current-script selection uses the mode starting level, clamps high levels to the last list item, and follows runtime exception paths for missing inputs.
Kill/night entry and general gameplay-state changes use the documented guards, PrevState update, and change event.
Standard setup processes Outcast, Minion, Demon, and Villager, filling each persistent roster toward max(base, disguised) without replacement from starting candidates.
Random roster selection prepares required/always roles, selects base faction quotas in Demon-Outcast-Minion-Villager order, refills empty pools, and returns a random-key shuffle.
The constructor stores allCharCount, towns, demons, outsiders, and minions at +0x10 through +0x20; disguised counts remain zero-initialized.
Always-in-deck routing uses the floating-point Demon-plus-Minion fraction and a strict Random.Range(0,1) comparison, while usually-disguised roles bypass bluff routing.
Roster insertion appends Villager, Outcast, Minion, and Demon roles to their persistent faction lists without deduplication.
Empty-pool refill ignores its input, appends Townsfolk-Outcasts-Minions-Townsfolk, removes one occurrence per in-play dataRef, and filters by exact faction while preserving remaining duplicates.

Handout resets mode-specific player resources, advances level and day counters, and starts the two-state setup coroutine; setup clears round state, selects and clones the script, and orders relic, roster, state, rule, board, and UI callbacks around a 0.1-second yield.

Board initialization disables every pool and scans all exact-size matches without an early break; board management constructs cards, publishes a new shallow list, runs Init and serialized ordered Start passes, invokes setup, and shuffles. The shipped 15-entry Start sequence, managed-role identity bindings, duplicate exceptions, and highest-ID-first duplicate order are pinned by serialized assets and native control flow.

Per-card initialization resets the observed fields, changes to Hidden and invokes the state callback before clearing statuses, while delayed reveal clones the role before a 0.3-second yield and then calls the internal Reveal routine.

The internal Reveal routine resolves register-as and bluff data, orders HealthyBluff, Init, and AfterRoundStart actions, presents real or bluff information, and refreshes without changing player reveal state or invoking onReveal.

The click dispatcher orders phase and picker gates, hidden reveal or Day actions, protection handling, and successful execution; Kill mutates state and dispatches callbacks before snapshotting reveal order, with hidden kills synchronously incrementing CurrentReveal through the kill event.

Run initialization requests Init before resetting day, deck, relics, faction lists, score, and levels, conditionally loads characters, and starts an iterator that yields once before OnGameInit and the mode-dependent OnGameStart or Map dispatch.

Character loading filters all character data by unlocked ID in source order and appends exact Villager, Outcast, Minion, and Demon values through Gameplay.Instance without clearing or deduplicating the destination lists.

Relic dispatch sends every trigger to every current relic; special-rule refresh removes and clears old rules, calls GetRules twice for nonempty role results, aggregates and initializes new rules, then emits OnSpecialRulesInit.
Normal reveal dispatch invokes the character-revealed multicast event before snapshotting CurrentReveal, while the configured Gameplay handler increments that global counter.

Forced real reveal changes presentation without normal reveal accounting; execution and kill/reveal helpers bypass killability and differ in Executed dispatch and final order resnapshot, while the protected helper only dispatches Protected and restores gameplay state.

Demon kill emits its pick VFX immediately, then after 0.45 seconds gates on Dead and killability before mutating death state, adding evil-source statuses, ordering card and role death actions, and dispatching kill bookkeeping.

Killed-character bookkeeping conditionally awards evil-kill score, appends without deduplication, updates UI, and tail-dispatches the end-condition event; the apparent jump-table warning is a delegate-call false positive.

Night flow launches only from Night, stably selects cards by first role-order index, waits 0.8 seconds then 0.4 seconds before each Night action and 0.8 seconds afterward, requests Day, resets the phase-local counter, and starts an unawaited fade-out.
Character action dispatch orders its special gate, callback, Start latch, lying decision, and real/bluff role calls; lying is derived from corruption or the non-HealthyBluff Evil/bluff conditions.
Default and Drunk wrong-execution costs are 5 and 2; signed value reduction clamps only below zero and invokes its change callback once after the store.
Default, Knight, and Doppelganger killability predicates and the Knight protected/executed side effects are documented from native control flow.
The delayed terminal predicate uses Saint, signed health, then raw evil-list counts in precedence order, and the win, loss, and delayed Summary paths have the documented event and UI ordering.
Status insertion uses exact resistance and duplicate checks, ignores the source, and replaces the single shared target reference after every non-resisted call.
Signed value addition clamps only above max after unchecked arithmetic and invokes its change callback once after the store.
Striga creates a threshold-four Night rule whose global subscriptions, reveal gates, callbacks, transition, counter reset, and duplicate lifecycle behavior are documented.
Striga applies demon-kill immunity at Start and at Night dispatches the preferred then fallback victim pipeline before dealing 2 player HP, with no reroll after delayed-kill rejection.

The selected non-Dead, register-as alignment, Hidden, and missing-active-status filters preserve order and multiplicity, while random selection performs one unguarded index draw without checking liveness.
Status and resistance insertion, the one shared cure target, virtual removal permission, default permission, and Drunk's Corrupted veto are documented from native control flow.

Truthful Plague Doctor Start filters the current board to apparent Villagers missing active Corrupted and exact Corrupted resistance, samples one uniformly, and adds only Corrupted with no self or liveness exclusion; an empty pool is a clean no-op.

Real and bluff Plague Doctor Day actions install distinct one-target callbacks with complete cancellation cleanup; picker completion preserves the selected list through callback dispatch, allows self and any clickable dead card, then clears selection and returns to Day. BluffAct has no Start branch and the role has no internal WorkingAbility gate.

Both Plague Doctor callbacks branch on raw active Corrupted presence: truth draws apparent Evil only for Corrupted, bluff draws apparent Good only for clean, neither alignment pool filters liveness or guards empty results, self always formats clean, and every emitted character list is [picked,result-or-null].

Plague Doctor has no Drunk-specific status exception: it observes only active Corrupted. A Chancellor-generated Drunk can nevertheless be genuinely clean when Character.Init preserves an earlier Alchemist resistance that blocks Drunk's self-targeted Corrupted insertion, reconciling asc84_v2 without suppressing Corrupted on every Drunk.
